meta.title: Hi, future 7th grader! Begin school in Eilat
meta.description: Meet Begin school in Eilat — for kids starting 7th grade (ז׳) in September and their parents: how the school works, what a day looks like, where everything is.
meta.ogAlt: The Begin school courtyard with its three red shade sails
meta.parentsDescription: Starting 7th grade at Begin school in Eilat: how the school is organised, safety, getting there, registration, and what we are still checking with the school.
meta.privacyDescription: This site uses no cookies, collects no data and runs no trackers.

ui.suggest: This site is available in English.

title: Hi there,
future 7th grader
hero.lead: At first, a new school is a bit of a blur: a big building, lots of teachers, no idea what's where. Scroll down — every screen gets a little sharper.

years.title: Six years, one school
years.lead: Begin runs from 7th grade (ז׳) to 12th (י״ב). After 9th grade you don't switch schools — you just move up to the upper school.

stage1.name: Middle school
stage1.text: A building of its own: its own entrance, its own office, its own teachers' room and counsellors.

stage2.name: Upper school
stage2.text: This is where you choose a major (מגמה) and prepare for the בגרות exams. That's a long way off — for now, just know the whole road runs through here.

changes.title: What changes after 6th grade
changes.lead: Lots of things will be new. That's true for everyone moving up to 7th grade — and it's completely fine.

items.was: One teacher for almost the whole day.
items.now: Lots of teachers, each with their own subject.

items.was: Your homeroom teacher is always around.
items.now: Every class has a מחנך or מחנכת — a homeroom teacher. You'll see them less in lessons, but they're your grown-up at school: you can go to them with any question.

items.was: When things are hard, you go to your teacher.
items.now: There's a יועצת — a school counsellor. You can talk to her when something is hard, scary or just confusing.
You get your own מערכת שעות — your timetable. It looks complicated in week one; after that you get used to it.

items.was: You've known your whole class since 1st grade.
items.now: Classes are made of kids from different schools. At first almost everyone is a stranger — and they don't know anyone either.
Tests (מבחנים) and a תעודה — a report card with grades.

changes.outro: In the first weeks everybody gets a bit lost. A month later you'll be the one showing others the way.

day.title: A day at Begin
day.lead: The school will announce the bell times. For now, let's just walk through the places where the day happens.

steps.title: Morning. The gate
steps.text: You come in from Malkat Shva Street (מלכת שבא). Above the gate is a sign with a portrait of Menachem Begin — the school is named after him.

steps.title: The courtyard
steps.text: A big inner courtyard: grass, benches and three red shade sails. Straight ahead is the entrance to the middle school.

steps.title: Lesson time
steps.text: Classrooms have names, not just numbers. This door says דולפין — dolphin.

steps.title: Break
steps.text: Shade under the sails, picnic tables, a chess table under the leaning tree. There's a kiosk in the courtyard too.

steps.title: The library
steps.text: A quiet place full of books, right behind the middle school lobby.

steps.title: Sport
steps.text: The “Toto Pais” sports hall (טוטו פיס) and a sports court next to the school.

steps.title: Home
steps.text: The bus stop “תיכון בגין / מלכת שבא” is right by the school.

names.lead: Here classrooms aren't just numbers. The door signs show birds, flowers, sea creatures, trees, places in the Negev and heroes of the Tanakh. Maybe your class will be called דולפין — Dolphin.

safe.title: It's safe here
safe.lead: Short and calm — the important things.

items.title: 4 safe rooms
items.text: The school has four safe rooms (ממ״ד): in the library, in the middle school and two in the upper school. The Begin Map shows the nearest one.

items.title: Evacuation plan
items.text: The school has an earthquake evacuation plan with assembly points.

items.title: A sign at the gate
items.text: “This school has a safe room open to the public” — that's what the sign at the entrance says.

items.title: Who to go to
items.text: If something happens or you feel scared — go to your מחנך, the יועצת or the school office.

kids.a: Everyone gets a bit lost in the first days. Ask any teacher or older student. You can also open the Begin Map on your phone: type the classroom name and it shows you the way.

kids.q: Will my friends from my school be there?
kids.a: Begin takes kids from different elementary schools in Eilat, so you'll probably see some familiar faces. The school decides who goes into which class. And new friends come quickly: everyone around you is new too.

kids.q: Who is my grown-up at school?
kids.a: Your homeroom teacher — the מחנך or מחנכת. There's also the יועצת, the school counsellor: you can talk to her about anything.

kids.q: When are the bells, and how many lessons?
kids.a: The school will publish the bell times. You'll get your own timetable (מערכת שעות) at the start of the year.

kids.q: What should I bring on the first day?
kids.a: The school will send a list. And in Eilat a bottle of water is always a good idea.

parents.q: How is a child placed in 7th grade?
parents.a: Under Ministry of Education rules, the local authority assigns pupils to middle schools and notifies parents. Please check the procedure and dates for Eilat with the municipality and the school.

parents.q: How do I contact the school?
parents.a: The Eilat municipality's list of schools gives Begin's phone number as {phone}.

parents.q: Is there support for new immigrants?
parents.a: The school plan shows a room called “אולפן” (ulpan). Please check with the school how support for newly arrived students works today.
There are four safe rooms (ממ״ד) and an earthquake evacuation plan. A sign at the gate says the school has a safe room open to the public.

parents.q: How will my child get there?
parents.a: The bus stop “תיכון בגין / מלכת שבא” is right by the school. There's parking by the gate, with accessible spaces.

school.title: The school
school.text: Begin High School (בית ספר תיכון ע״ש מנחם בגין), Eilat, is a six-year state school (ממלכתי), named after Menachem Begin, Israel's sixth Prime Minister. It has two parts: the middle school (חטיבת ביניים, grades ז׳–ט׳) in its own building with its own entrance and office, and the upper school (חטיבה עליונה, grades י׳–י״ב).

transition.title: What changes in 7th grade
transition.text: Instead of one class teacher there are subject teachers. Each class has a homeroom teacher (מחנך/מחנכת), and the school has counsellors (יועצות). Students get a personal timetable (מערכת שעות), tests and a report card (תעודה). Classes are made up of children from different elementary schools.
tips: Ask your child what worries them most — often it's something small, like “where are the toilets?”
Walk the way from home to the gate together before the year starts.
Open the Begin Map together and find the key places: the middle school entrance, the library, the safe room.

registration.title: Registration and placement
registration.text: Under the Ministry of Education circular (0386), the local authority assigns elementary school graduates to middle schools and notifies parents. Please check how and when this works in Eilat this year with the municipality and the school.

safety.title: Safety
safety.text: Four safe rooms (ממ״ד): in the library, in the middle school and two in the upper school. An earthquake evacuation plan with assembly points. At the main gate, a sign about a safe room open to the public.

route.title: Getting there
route.text: Malkat Shva Street (מלכת שבא). The bus stop “תיכון בגין / מלכת שבא” is right by the school. Parking by the gate, with accessible spaces.
route.addressNote: Sources give different house numbers (2 and 28) — we're checking with the school.

olim.title: For new immigrants
olim.text: The school plan shows a room called “אולפן” (ulpan). Whether there is currently a Hebrew programme and support for new students — please ask the school. This site is also available in Russian and Arabic, so feel free to share it.

privacy.lead: In short: we don't collect anything about you.

items.title: No cookies, no tracking
items.text: The site sets no cookies and uses no analytics, ads or visit counters.

items.title: No forms
items.text: There are no forms that collect information about children or adults.

items.title: What your browser stores
items.text: Only two of your choices — language and “animation on/off”. They stay in your browser's localStorage and are never sent anywhere. Clearing the site's data removes them.

items.title: Fonts and images
items.text: Everything loads from this site itself, with no third-party servers.

items.title: External links
items.text: Links to Google Maps, Waze, the Begin Map and the municipality website lead to other sites with their own rules.

items.title: Hosting
items.text: The site is hosted on GitHub Pages. GitHub may keep technical logs (such as IP addresses) under its own privacy policy.

privacy.contact: Questions about the site can be asked in the project's GitHub repository.
